What happens to my LinkedIn when I die?

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 15 Oct 2026

Short answer: LinkedIn offers two options: close the account or memorialise the profile. Anyone connected or related by last name can report a member as deceased, and LinkedIn will memorialise the profile. Closing the account requires someone with legal authority to act for the estate, a death certificate and probate-type documents. LinkedIn never gives out passwords.

Key facts

  • Memorialise: report as deceased (connection or same surname)
  • Close: needs legal authority
  • Memorialised accounts are locked
  • Data deleted within 30 days of closure

How do I prepare my LinkedIn account?

  1. Submit LinkedIn's request form for a deceased member.
  2. Provide the member's name, profile URL, relationship and, if needed, proof of death.
  3. Download your own data now from Settings → Data privacy → Get a copy of your data.

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • Member's full name, profile URL and your relationship
  • Helpful: their email, date of death and an obituary link
  • To close: death certificate plus Letters of Administration, Letters Testamentary, Letters of Representation or another court order

How long does it take?

After closure, LinkedIn says it can take up to 30 days to fully delete the data.

What can't be recovered?

  • Login access and messages
  • All profile data after closure

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my LinkedIn when I die?

LinkedIn offers two options: close the account or memorialise the profile. Anyone connected or related by last name can report a member as deceased, and LinkedIn will memorialise the profile. Closing the account requires someone with legal authority to act for the estate, a death certificate and probate-type documents. LinkedIn never gives out passwords.

Will LinkedIn delete a dead person's profile?

Yes, on request. LinkedIn can memorialise or close it.

Can family get a LinkedIn password?

No. LinkedIn says it won't disclose usernames or passwords to anyone, including family, under any circumstances.

What's the difference between memorialising and closing?

Memorialising keeps the profile visible but locked; closing deletes it. Closing requires legal authority.
